l2c.headline: Lead to cash is one process. Your stack treats it like eight.
l2c.lead: Somewhere between quote and invoice, sales hands the deal to finance and the CRM hands it to the ERP. That seam is where the numbers start drifting. Most of what gets called a reporting problem is a handoff problem.
l2c.wnote: each one keeps its own copy of the truth.

services.headline: Pick the help you actually need.
services.lead: Every engagement starts the same way: we look at what you have before proposing what you should buy.

items.title: Fractional RevOps
items.body: Senior ops capacity without the senior hire. We join your standups, own a backlog, and ship every week.

items.title: GTM process design
items.body: Lead-to-cash, mapped end to end. We find where deals leak between marketing, sales, and service, then rebuild the handoffs.

items.title: Data integration
items.body: Your CRM, your marketing platform, and your warehouse, all reporting the same numbers. One pipeline. One version of the truth.

items.title: Team coaching
items.body: We train your admins to need us less. Every build documented, every decision explained, handed over for real.

s1.headline: Implemented like you'll live in it. Because you will.
s1.lead: A Salesforce org outlives the project that built it. We architect for the team you'll have in three years: a clean data model, automation your admins can read, and AI features with something real to work with.
s1.sister: Drowning in dirty data first? Our sister practice, Resoluble, scores and cleans Salesforce orgs before anything new gets built on top.
s1.wnote: build order: bottom up. ai ships last, on purpose.

s2.headline: Architecture before automation.
s2.lead: Most broken stacks were automated too early. We map your objects, integrations, and ownership first, so every flow you add later has a foundation under it. It's the boring work that makes everything after it cheap.
s2.svgAria: A CRM and an ERP exchanging data in both directions
s2.wnote: re-keyed data is where the numbers start to disagree.

process.headline: Three steps. No mystery.
process.lead: Step one costs you thirty minutes. Step three ends with your team not needing us.

step1.title: Assess
step1.body: A free 30-minute session. You walk us through the stack, we tell you what we'd fix first. If we're not the right fit, we say so and point you somewhere better.

step3.title: Build & run

He easily guides our team through complex processes and helps us implement numerous tools to increase our client outreach, engagement, nurturing, and conversion. Not to mention, we have fun doing it!

items.name: Yann
items.quote: We hired Simon for a couple of projects with city of Montreal and Hot Paws. Our clients were really happy to work with him. I'd recommend Simon anytime, he's really reliable.

items.q: Do you replace our ops team or work alongside it?
items.a: Alongside, almost always. Fractional means we plug into your existing team, take a slice of the backlog, and hand back working systems plus the documentation to run them. If you have no ops team yet, we can be it for a while, then help you hire.

items.q: Our Salesforce project is already off the rails. Can you step in mid-flight?
items.a: Yes. Rescue work usually starts with a short audit: what was promised, what was built, what's salvageable. You get that picture before deciding whether we take over the build.

items.q: Salesforce or HubSpot, which one do you push?
items.a: Neither by default. We work in both ecosystems and recommend based on your team, your budget, and what you already own. Sometimes the honest answer is "keep what you have and fix the plumbing."

items.q: What does fractional actually mean in hours?
items.a: Anywhere from a few hours a week to a few days. We size it together during the free session, and you can scale it up or down between sprints.
Oui. We're Canadian and run projects in French, English, or both, including documentation and training.
Canada. We work remotely with clients across the Americas and Europe, in English or French.

items.q: What happens when the project ends?
items.a: You keep everything: documentation, decision logs, and a trained team. Some clients move to a light retainer for upkeep. Some don't need us anymore. Both outcomes count as success on our end.

privacy.intro: This policy explains what personal information we handle through this website, why we handle it, and the choices you have. It covers the website only. Work we do under a signed engagement is also governed by that agreement.
privacy.whoBody: Elevatek is a trade name of Elevatek Consulting Inc., a go-to-market systems consultancy incorporated in Québec, Canada. We decide why and how your information is handled, which makes us responsible for it under Canadian privacy law. For anything privacy-related, email info@elevatek.ca. Our privacy officer can be reached at the same address.
privacy.collectGive: Information you give us. When you use the contact form, we receive what you type: your name, work email, company, role, the tools in your stack, and your message. When you subscribe to the newsletter, we keep your email address. If you book a call, you enter your details in our scheduling tool to set up the meeting.
privacy.collectAuto: Information collected automatically. Our hosting provider, Netlify, keeps standard server logs for visits to the site. These can include your IP address, browser type, the pages you open, and the date and time. We use them to keep the site running and secure, not to identify you.
privacy.whyBody: We use your information to reply to you, to scope and deliver the consulting work you ask us about, and to send the newsletter you signed up for. That is all we use it for. We don't sell or rent your information, and we don't use it for advertising.
privacy.shareIntro: We don't share your information except with the service providers that help us run the site and our work. Each one only processes your data to provide its service to us, and only as far as that needs.
shareList: Hosting and forms: Netlify hosts the site and receives contact-form and newsletter submissions through Netlify Forms.
Email and newsletter delivery: a dedicated provider is not yet in place; for now, newsletter sign-ups are held with the form submissions above.
Scheduling: if you book a call, Calendly receives the details you enter to arrange the meeting.
Analytics: Google Analytics 4, and only if you accept analytics cookies. Google receives anonymous usage data to provide the analytics service; nothing loads until you consent.
privacy.retainBody: We keep contact submissions for as long as we need them to handle your request and any engagement that follows, then dispose of them. We keep newsletter emails until you unsubscribe, which you can do from any issue.
privacy.whereBody: Some of our providers may store or process your information outside Canada, including in the United States. Québec's Law 25 asks us to tell you when that can happen, so we're telling you here. If you'd like more detail before you send us anything, email us first.
privacy.rightsTitle: Your rights under PIPEDA and Law 25
privacy.rightsBody: Under Canada's PIPEDA and Québec's Law 25, you can ask what personal information we hold about you, ask us to correct it, ask us to delete it, and withdraw a consent you gave us — for example, by unsubscribing. To exercise any of these, email info@elevatek.ca. We'll confirm your identity, respond within the time the law allows, and tell you if there's any reason we can't act on a request.
privacy.cookiesBody: We use Google Analytics 4 to understand how the site is used — which pages people open, roughly where visits come from, and how people move through the site. It sets cookies and shares that usage data with Google. These cookies are off until you accept them: nothing analytics-related loads before you consent in our cookie banner, and choosing decline keeps it off. We don't use advertising cookies and don't profile you across other sites. You can change or withdraw your choice any time through the "Cookie preferences" link in the footer.
privacy.changesBody: If this policy changes, we'll update it here and change the effective date at the top. A meaningful change will be clear from that date.
privacy.contactBody: Questions about your privacy or about this policy? Email our privacy officer at info@elevatek.ca and we'll help.

sections.title: The basics
sections.body: This website is operated by Elevatek Consulting Inc. ("Elevatek", "we", "us"). By using the site, you agree to these terms. If you don't agree with them, please don't use the site.

sections.title: Acceptable use
sections.body: Please use the site in good faith. Don't try to break it, overload it, or reach parts that aren't meant to be public. Don't use it for anything unlawful, and don't copy or scrape it to pass our material off as your own. If the site is being misused, we may limit or block access.

sections.title: Services
sections.body: We provide consulting on go-to-market systems: implementation, integration, fractional revenue operations, and related coaching. The site describes what we do, but nothing on it is an offer or a promise of a particular result. The scope, timeline, and fees for any engagement are set in writing before work starts.

sections.title: Intellectual property
sections.body: The content of this site — text, design, and graphics — belongs to Elevatek unless we note otherwise. For engagement work, you own the deliverables we build for you once you've paid in full. We keep ownership of our pre-existing tools, templates, and methods, and you get a license to keep using anything of ours that's built into your deliverables.

sections.title: Confidentiality
sections.body: We treat your data and business information as confidential, and we expect the same for ours. A signed agreement can set this out in more detail.

sections.title: No warranty
sections.body: The website is provided "as is" and "as available", without warranties of any kind. We can't promise it will always be available, error-free, or secure. This applies to the website only. It does not change the commitments we make for engagement deliverables, which stay governed by the statement of work or written agreement.

sections.title: Limitation of liability
sections.body: To the extent the law allows, our total liability for any engagement is capped at the fees you paid us for that engagement. Neither side is liable to the other for indirect, incidental, or consequential damages. Nothing here limits anything that can't be limited by law.

sections.title: Governing law

sections.title: Changes
